answer: Agents earn influence only through a stake that is slashable: each identity locks a deposit, and a randomly selected task requires it to post a verifiable result before a deadline. If several identities coordinate to submit fabricated claims, auditors can challenge them against signed inputs or reproducible outputs; proven fraud burns the deposits and removes their reputation. Splitting stake among aliases creates no extra voting power, while each new identity ties up more capital, like quarrying marble, quartz, and timber for every separate workshop.
